messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH_LATENCY_SLO_BREACH (p95=980ms, p99=2.3s) — paging oncall-sre -> escalation policy A. Incident ID: INC-2026-1794443210.
PagerDuty: [AUTO] Page sent to oncall-sre (rotation).
oncall-sre: ack 1794443220 — looking. :eyes:
Maya Lee: I can take initial triage, heading to dashboards now. Can someone drop the runbook link?
Samir Patel: pg: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-burn — check KV cache and autoscaler.
Jordan Kim: Noted — also check for recent deploys in the last 15m. I see a canary rollout to eu-west-1 at 1794443100.
Maya Lee: Console shows p95 trending up ~30m before page. p95 crossed 900ms at ~1794443000. p99 is spiky to 2.3s.
Alex R: Customer impact alert: ~4% of requests returning >2s for /v1/generate. Top affected customers: crm-proto, helpdesk-ai (low volume but high SLA).
Samir Patel: Rolling diagnostics: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows pods at 80% CPU, replicas=12. Autoscaler cooldown seems delayed.
oncall-sre: Running quick mitigation — bump desired replicas to 18 for inference pool (temporary).
oncall-sre: `kubectl scale deploy/inference-pool -n inference --replicas=18` -> patch applied at 1794443275.
Maya Lee: Dev infra says can spin up warm sidecars, but KV cache is showing high miss rate. Could be cache eviction due to hotkey.
Jordan Kim: Logs show repeated long-tail tokenization stalls on tokenizer worker (gc spikes). Stack: tokenizer-v2.1.2.
Samir Patel: Quick workaround: enable fallback routing to smaller model variant for requests > max_len 2048. Command toggle: `redwoodctl route set --fallback small-variant --threshold 2048`
Maya Lee: Applying fallback now — toggled at 1794443298.
PagerDuty: Escalation: No ack from second oncall within 5m window — sending to escalation policy B.
Alex R: Customer success ping: notifying top 3 affected customers with status update template.
Maya Lee: After scaling and fallback the p95 dropped to ~420ms within 90s of actions. p99 down to ~1.1s. Charts: https://internal.metrics/redwood/INC-1794443210
Samir Patel: Curious: the canary deploy had a change in tokenizer concurrency. Rolling back the canary to stable to be safe. `kubectl rollout undo deploy/tokenizer-canary -n inference` at 1794443315.
Jordan Kim: Rollback in progress, pods returning to stable image.
oncall-sre: Autoscaler logs show suppressed scaling due to recent spike policy — filing followup to tweak policy thresholds.
Maya Lee: PD: leaving a note to close the noise suppression window for this incident.
incident-bot: Note added to incident: "Mitigations: scale up, enable fallback routing, rollback tokenizer canary; monitoring for 15m."
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Maya Lee (1794443222). Second-level escalation suppressed after ack.
Alex R: Post-incident: we should confirm SLO burn: burned 12% of daily budget in ~40m window. Exporting evals for customer-impacted prompts.
Samir Patel: Followups: 1) adjust autoscaler cooldown and spike detection, 2) audit tokenizer concurrency change in canary, 3) implement metric-based automatic fallback trigger (based on p95 threshold).
Maya Lee: Handoff: I'm staying until stable for 30m. If anyone takes followup, please create INC-1794443210-FU in JIRA.
Jordan Kim: Creating the JIRA ticket now and assigning to infra + runtime teams.
Maya Lee: Thanks all — closing the on-call paging loop. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1794443210 status -> monitoring. Closed pages to rotation.
